howToUse: 1. Attach or paste your lecture slides (PDF/PPTX), notes, code files, or subject syllabus along with this JSON file into your AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.).
2. Instruct the AI: 'Follow _aiPrompt strictly to generate a complete quiz based on my attached material using this exact JSON structure.'
3. Copy or save the raw JSON returned by the AI (without _aiPrompt) and upload it in Quiz Manager -> Import JSON.
_aiPrompt.prompt:
You are an expert educator, psychometric assessment designer, and strict JSON generator for Quiz Platform. Using ONLY the attached slides, notes, syllabus, or specified subject, generate a high-rigor, deeply engaging assessment in strict JSON format matching the schema below.

SOURCE GROUNDING & PEDAGOGICAL QUALITY:
- Anchor 100% of questions directly in concepts, definitions, formulas, diagrams, edge cases, comparisons, and code examples present in the provided slides or subject. Never invent unrelated trivia.
- Progress difficulty thoughtfully across Bloom's taxonomy (concept recall -> comprehension -> code/process tracing -> edge-case analysis & synthesis).
- Craft 4 plausible options for multiple-choice questions that are parallel in grammar and similar in length (do NOT make the correct option noticeably longer or more detailed). Each distractor must reflect a realistic student misconception.
- Write concise, teaching-focused explanations (1-3 sentences) explaining WHY the correct answer works AND why the main trap option is wrong.

PLATFORM FEATURE UTILIZATION:
- Actively mix supported question types where they fit the content: 'multiple-choice', 'code-output' (both with 4 terminal options and free-text stdout prediction), 'text' (short answer with accepted aliases array), 'ordering' (process/execution/hierarchy sequences), 'matching' (term-to-definition pairs), and 'compiler' (for coding topics, ALWAYS set BOTH type='compiler' AND isCompiler=true with complete working referenceCode).
- Group questions logically using the 'part' field (e.g., 'Part 1: Core Concepts', 'Part 2: Tracing & Analysis', 'Part 3: Applied Engineering').
- Scale 'points' by cognitive demand (10 = recall, 15 = trace/short-answer, 20 = ordering/matching, 25 = coding challenge).

UI & TEXT RENDERING RULES (CRITICAL):
- Question text, options, orderingItems, matchingPairs, and explanation are rendered by KaTeX-aware plain text (MathRenderer). Wrap math, Big-O, and formulas in KaTeX delimiters ($...$ inline or $$...$$ display, escaping backslashes in JSON like \\log, \\frac).
- NEVER put Markdown syntax (**bold**, *italic*, ### headings, ```code blocks```, or `inline backticks`) in question, options, orderingItems, matchingPairs, or explanation—raw backticks and asterisks appear literally in the UI!
- Put code snippets strictly inside 'codeSnippet' (for 'code-output') or 'compilerConfig' (for 'compiler'), using properly escaped \n newlines.
- Store 'orderingItems' in the EXACT CORRECT target sequence (up to 5-6 concise items <= 65 chars each); the platform shuffles them automatically.
- Store 'matchingPairs' with concise 'left' terms (<= 35 chars) and crisp 'right' definitions (<= 65 chars); 4 pairs is ideal.
- For 'text' questions, prefer short canonical answers (1-3 words) and optionally provide a string array of accepted variations (e.g. ["len", "len()"]). Remember the platform grades text answers with 70% fuzzy matching.

STRICT JSON OUTPUT:
- Return ONLY valid raw JSON matching { "quizzes": [ { ... } ] }. Do NOT include '_aiPrompt', comments, trailing commas, or prose outside the JSON.

rootObject.quizzes: QuizObject[] (1 or more quiz objects; omitting _aiPrompt)

QuizObject.id: string (optional lowercase kebab-case slug; auto-generated if omitted)
QuizObject.title: string (required, concise clear assessment title)
QuizObject.questionsPerAttempt: number (set equal to questions.length for full quiz)
QuizObject.isProctored: boolean (true for formal exams, false for practice)
QuizObject.strictTabSwitchLimit: number (0 = unlimited, e.g. 2-3 for proctored exams)
QuizObject.reviewMode: boolean (true shows immediate feedback after each question)
QuizObject.questions: QuestionObject[] (recommended 8-15 questions tailored to slide count)

QuestionObject.question: string (required, clean prompt text + optional $KaTeX$; NO raw markdown ** or ``` or `)
QuestionObject.explanation: string (clear explanation of why correct answer is right and distractors fail)
QuestionObject.options: string[] (required for multiple-choice [4 options]; optional 4 choices for code-output MCQ mode)
QuestionObject.correctAnswer: number (0-based index for MCQ / code-output-with-options) | string (exact stdout for free code-output or text) | string[] (accepted synonyms for text)
QuestionObject.codeSnippet: string (required for code-output; valid runnable/traceable snippet with \n)
QuestionObject.orderingItems: string[] (required for ordering; MUST be in the exact correct order top-to-bottom)
QuestionObject.matchingPairs: { left: string, right: string }[] (required for matching; 3-5 clean pairs)

compilerConfig.referenceCode: string (REQUIRED complete working solution when isCompiler is true)
compilerConfig.testCases: { input: string, expectedOutput: string, isHidden: boolean }[]

QuestionObject.imageUrl: string (optional valid https image URL ONLY if you have a real diagram/image URL)
QuestionObject.videoUrl: string (optional valid YouTube/MP4 URL ONLY if referencing an actual lecture video)
QuestionObject.videoTimestamp: number (optional start second if videoUrl is set)

recommendedCountsFromSlides.shortDeck_1_to_10_slides: 8-10 mixed questions covering every slide section
recommendedCountsFromSlides.standardDeck_11_to_25_slides: 12-16 questions across all sections with multiple parts
recommendedCountsFromSlides.fullUnit_26_plus_slides: 18-25 questions with balanced recall, tracing, ordering, matching & coding

quizzes.title: Algorithms, Data Structures & Complexity Mastery
quizzes.description: Balanced multi-format assessment covering asymptotic analysis, Python runtime behavior, networking layers, HTTP semantics, and practical coding.

questions.question: On a sorted array of size $N$, what is the tight worst-case time complexity of binary search, and what is $\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\log_2 N}{N}$?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the remaining search interval at each comparison, giving $O(\log N)$ time. Because $N$ grows strictly faster than $\log_2 N$, their ratio approaches $0$ as $N \to \infty$.

questions.question: Predict the exact stdout printed by this Python comprehension and string join snippet:
questions.codeSnippet:
data = [i ** 2 for i in range(6) if i % 2 == 1]
print('-'.join(map(str, data)))
questions.explanation: In range(6), the odd values are 1, 3, and 5. Squaring each produces [1, 9, 25], and joining them with '-' prints 1-9-25.

questions.question: What does this Python list-aliasing snippet print? Choose the exact terminal output:
questions.codeSnippet:
items = [10, 20, 30]
copy_ref = items
items = items + [40]
print(len(copy_ref), len(items))
questions.explanation: Reassigning items = items + [40] creates a new 4-element list bound to items, while copy_ref continues pointing to the original 3-element list (unlike .append(), which mutates in place).

questions.question: Which built-in Python function returns the number of elements inside a list, string, tuple, or dictionary?
questions.explanation: Calling len(collection) returns the integer count of items in constant $O(1)$ time for Python built-in containers.

questions.question: Order these OSI reference model layers from lowest physical layer (Layer 1) to highest application layer (Layer 7):
questions.explanation: Bottom-up encapsulation moves from bits (Physical) to frames (Data Link), packets (Network), segments (Transport), and finally user-facing protocols (Application).

questions.question: Match each HTTP response status code with its standard meaning:

matchingPairs.right: Client cached copy is still fresh

questions.explanation: 2xx confirms success, 3xx directs caching/redirects, 4xx flags client authorization or request errors (403 is forbidden even when known), and 5xx indicates server failures.

questions.explanation: Filter numbers where n % 2 == 0 and sum them. Using a generator expression runs in $O(N)$ time and $O(1)$ extra space.

questions.question: What key advantage distinguishes non-blocking asynchronous I/O from synchronous blocking I/O on a single-threaded event loop?
options: Pending I/O operations yield control back to the event loop so other tasks run meanwhile
Every I/O request spawns an isolated hardware CPU core automatically
Network round-trip physical latency drops to zero milliseconds
The runtime disables garbage collection until all sockets close
questions.explanation: Async I/O does not reduce physical network latency or allocate extra CPU cores; instead it frees the thread from waiting idle while the OS notifies the event loop upon completion.
